test_cases.test_case: Rapid double-click Add to cart on a single product

test_cases.test_case: Click Add then immediately click Remove before initial action completes

test_cases.test_case: Attempt to add product when product is already in cart (Add button should not be available)
preconditions: User is on Product Detail page context
Product is already in the Shopping Cart (entity_state == In Cart)
steps: 1. Navigate to the Product Detail page for the product that is already in the cart

test_cases.test_case: Attempt to remove product when product is not in cart (Remove button should not be available)

test_cases.test_case: Rapid double-click Add to cart should not create duplicate cart entries
preconditions: Product Detail page is open for a product
The product's current entity_state is Not In Cart
steps: 1. Click the "Add to cart" button
2. Immediately (before UI finishes updating) click the "Add to cart" button again
3. Click the "Cart icon" link to navigate to the Shopping Cart page
4. Observe the Shopping Cart page and return to Product Detail
test_cases.expected_result: First Add to cart action succeeds; the immediate second click is ignored/blocked so no duplicate entry is created. Shopping Cart displays only one entry for that product. Product Detail action bar shows the In Cart state (button now reads "Remove").

test_cases.test_case: Rapid Add then immediate Remove (consecutive state transitions) yields a stable final state
preconditions: Product Detail page is open for a product
The product's current entity_state is Not In Cart
steps: 1. Click the "Add to cart" button
2. Immediately click the "Remove" button (before or as the Add finishes)
3. Observe the Product Detail action bar state
4. Click the "Cart icon" link to open the Shopping Cart page and verify contents
test_cases.expected_result: The rapid Add then Remove sequence succeeds as discrete state transitions; final visible state on Product Detail is Not In Cart (button reads "Add to cart"). Shopping Cart does not contain the product after the sequence (the Remove succeeded and no duplicate entries were created).

test_cases.test_case: Start Add to cart then immediately navigate Back to products

The product's current entity_state is Not In Cart
steps: 1. Click the "Add to cart" button
2. Immediately click the "Back to products" link
3. On the Product Inventory page, locate the same product and observe its cart indicator/button
4. Optionally click the product to re-open Product Detail and observe the action bar state
test_cases.expected_result: The Add to cart action succeeds before navigation cancels it; on Product Inventory the product shows the In Cart indicator (or the action bar on re-opened Product Detail shows "Remove"). Navigation did not create duplicate cart entries. (Action succeeds.)

test_cases.test_case: Navigate to Shopping Cart after add, then press browser Back — ensure no duplicate add on back

The product's current entity_state is Not In Cart
steps: 1. Click the "Add to cart" button
2. Click the "Cart icon" link to navigate to the Shopping Cart page
3. Use the browser Back button to return to the Product Detail page
4. Click the "Cart icon" link again to re-open the Shopping Cart page and observe contents
test_cases.expected_result: Adding the product succeeds and pressing Back does not cause an additional add. Product Detail shows In Cart state after going back. Shopping Cart still shows only one entry for that product (no duplicate entries were created by navigation).

test_cases.test_case: Rapid double-click Remove when product is In Cart should not cause errors or multiple removals

test_cases.expected_result: First Remove action succeeds; the immediate second click is ignored/blocked so no inconsistent state occurs. Shopping Cart does not contain the product after the remove. Product Detail action bar shows Not In Cart state (button reads "Add to cart").

test_cases.test_case: Rapid double-click of Finish on Overview
preconditions: User is signed in (if required) and on the Checkout - Overview step
Cart is populated and payment & shipping information are displayed
steps: 1. Ensure the Overview page is visible with the Finish button in view
2. Click the Finish button
3. Immediately click the Finish button again (within a fraction of a second)
test_cases.expected_result: Second click is ignored / blocked; user is navigated to the confirmation page only once and no second navigation or duplicated confirmation UI appears. The UI shows the confirmation page on success.

test_cases.test_case: Press browser Back after successful Finish then attempt to Finish again
preconditions: User is on Checkout - Overview and Finish has not yet been clicked
Cart and payment/shipping info are present
steps: 1. Click the Finish button
2. Wait until the confirmation page loads
3. Use the browser Back button to return to the Checkout - Overview page
4. Attempt to click the Finish button again
test_cases.expected_result: Second submission attempt is blocked; clicking Finish after returning via browser Back does not create a second successful completion. The UI either prevents the action (button disabled) or shows a visible inline message indicating the order cannot be re-submitted; user is not navigated to a second confirmation page.

test_cases.test_case: Click Cancel immediately after clicking Finish (race between Finish and Cancel)
preconditions: User is on Checkout - Overview with cart, payment, and shipping info displayed
steps: 1. Click the Finish button
2. Immediately click the Cancel button before navigation completes
test_cases.expected_result: Race resolved deterministically by the UI: either Finish completes and user is navigated to confirmation (Cancel click is ignored) or Cancel takes precedence and user exits checkout. The UI must show one clear outcome — either the confirmation page (Finish succeeds) or the post-cancel exit state — and must not leave the user in an intermediate/inconsistent state.

test_cases.test_case: Very long shipping/payment text shown on Overview (display/overflow handling)
preconditions: User has a cart and the shipping address and payment name fields contain very long values (200+ characters)
User has navigated to Checkout - Overview
steps: 1. View the shipping information section on the Overview step
2. View the payment information section on the Overview step
test_cases.expected_result: Overview display handles long text safely: long shipping/payment fields are either visibly truncated with an affordance to view the full value (e.g., ellipsis + 'Show more') or cause the content area to allow scrolling without breaking layout. There is a visible indicator if truncation occurs; the UI remains usable.

test_cases.test_case: Click Back Home from Confirmation clears cart and returns to Product Inventory
preconditions: User logged in as <role>
Confirmation page is open showing an order success message
steps: 1. Click the 'Back Home' button on the Confirmation page
test_cases.expected_result: Product Inventory page is displayed and the shopping cart is cleared: no items are listed in the cart and the cart badge shows 0 items

test_cases.test_case: Back Home button non-functional (no navigation and cart not cleared)
preconditions: User has completed checkout and is on the Confirmation page
There are <items in the cart> immediately prior to confirmation (cart contains items)
steps: 1. On the Confirmation page, verify the success message is visible
2. Click the 'Back Home' button
test_cases.expected_result: No navigation occurs; the user remains on the Confirmation page showing the success message; the cart is NOT cleared (cart still contains <items in the cart> as indicated by the cart badge or cart view); the 'Back Home' button remains visible. The on_success behaviour 'navigates to Product Inventory and clears the cart' did not occur.

test_cases.test_case: Navigation succeeds but cart is not cleared (partial failure)
preconditions: User has completed checkout and is on the Confirmation page
There are <items in the cart> immediately prior to confirmation (cart contains items)
steps: 1. On the Confirmation page, verify the success message is visible
2. Click the 'Back Home' button
test_cases.expected_result: The app navigates to the Product Inventory page but the cart was NOT cleared: the cart icon/badge on Product Inventory still displays <items in the cart> (or the cart view still lists the items). The on_success requirement to both navigate to Product Inventory AND clear the cart is only partially fulfilled; clearing the cart failed.

test_cases.test_case: Rapid double-click of Back Home while navigation is in progress
preconditions: User is on the Confirmation Page displaying the success message
steps: 1. Click the Back Home button once
2. Immediately click the Back Home button a second time before the first navigation completes
test_cases.expected_result: First click succeeds: UI navigates to Product Inventory and the cart is cleared. The immediate second click is ignored (no additional navigation or error). Product Inventory is displayed once and the cart remains cleared; no duplicate side-effects occur.

test_cases.test_case: Click Back Home when the cart is already empty
preconditions: User is on the Confirmation Page
The user's cart is already empty prior to clicking Back Home
steps: 1. Click the Back Home button
test_cases.expected_result: Navigation to Product Inventory succeeds; the cart remains empty and no error message is shown. Product Inventory displays with an empty cart.

test_cases.test_case: Press browser Back immediately after clicking Back Home (rapid re-navigation)
preconditions: User is on the Confirmation Page
steps: 1. Click the Back Home button
2. Immediately press the browser Back button
test_cases.expected_result: Clicking Back Home succeeds: UI navigates to Product Inventory and the cart is cleared. Immediately pressing Back does not re-trigger the cart-clear side-effect. If the Confirmation Page is restored from history, it is shown as a cached page and no additional server-side clear runs; cart remains cleared and no error is shown.

test_cases.test_case: Open Back Home in a new tab (middle-click / open in new tab)
preconditions: User is on the Confirmation Page
steps: 1. Open the Back Home action in a new browser tab (middle-click or context menu -> open in new tab)
2. Switch to the newly opened tab
test_cases.expected_result: Opening Back Home in a new tab succeeds: the new tab displays Product Inventory and the user's cart is cleared in-session. The original tab either remains on Confirmation Page or reflects the cleared cart; no inconsistent session state or error is shown and no duplicate side-effects occur.

test_cases.test_case: Click Logout button redirects to Login page
preconditions: User logged in as <role>
Logout button is visible in the application header
steps: 1. Click the Logout button in the header
test_cases.expected_result: ends session and redirects to Login page. The Login page is displayed with the login form visible.

test_cases.test_case: Attempt to invoke Logout while not authenticated (precondition not met)
preconditions: User is not logged in
steps: 1. Open the application in a new browser session where no user is logged in
2. In the browser address bar, navigate to the application's Logout URL (or click any visible Logout link/button if present)
test_cases.expected_result: Navigation is blocked/redirected: the Login page is displayed (login form visible). The Logout action is not performed because the precondition 'user must be logged in' is not met; no protected page is shown.

test_cases.test_case: Click Logout a second time after already logging out (idempotent/precondition timing)
preconditions: User is logged in as <role>
steps: 1. Log in as <role>
2. Click the Logout button
3. After the app redirects to the Login page, attempt to click Logout again (or navigate to the Logout URL) without logging in
test_cases.expected_result: Second Logout attempt is blocked/treated as no-op: the Login page remains displayed (login form visible). No error or protected page is presented; the system does not transition to an authenticated state and no unexpected behavior occurs. This verifies the precondition 'user must be logged in' prevents a logout action when already logged out.

test_cases.test_case: Access protected page (inventory) after Logout is performed
preconditions: User is logged in as <role>
steps: 1. Log in as <role>
2. Click the Logout button
3. From the Login page, attempt to navigate to the Inventory page (e.g., enter /inventory or click an Inventory link)
test_cases.expected_result: Access is blocked: the user is redirected to the Login page (login form visible); the Inventory page is not displayed. This confirms the consequence 'protected pages are not accessible without logging in again' after logout.

test_cases.test_case: Rapid double-click of Logout button
preconditions: User is logged in and on a protected page
steps: 1. Ensure the protected page is visible (user is authenticated)
2. Click the Logout button once
3. Immediately click the Logout button again (double-click / second click before redirect completes)
test_cases.expected_result: First click succeeds: session ends and the user is redirected to the Login page. The immediate second click is ignored or treated as a no-op; no duplicate logout errors are shown and no additional sessions are created (no visible error).

test_cases.test_case: Use browser Back button after successful logout
preconditions: User is logged in and on a protected page
steps: 1. Click the Logout button
2. Observe redirection to the Login page
3. Press the browser Back button once
test_cases.expected_result: Navigation back is blocked / error shown: the protected page is not displayed. The user remains on the Login page or is immediately redirected back to the Login page; protected content is not accessible without re-authentication.

test_cases.test_case: Logout while the browser is offline (network interruption)
preconditions: User is logged in and on a protected page
Ability to toggle the browser/network offline mode
steps: 1. Toggle the browser to offline mode (simulate network loss)
2. Click the Logout button
3. Toggle the browser back to online mode
test_cases.expected_result: Logout attempt is blocked / error shown while offline: a visible network error/toast is displayed and the user remains authenticated in the current tab. After returning online, the user may need to click Logout again; no silent session termination should be assumed while offline.

test_cases.test_case: Logout in one tab then immediately logout in another tab without refreshing
preconditions: User is logged in in two browser tabs (Tab A and Tab B) viewing protected pages
steps: 1. In Tab A, click the Logout button
2. Without refreshing Tab B, switch to Tab B and click the Logout button
test_cases.expected_result: First click (Tab A) succeeds: session ends and Tab A is redirected to the Login page. The subsequent logout click in Tab B is blocked / error shown or treated as a no-op: Tab B should either be redirected to the Login page or show that the session is no longer authenticated, with no server error displayed.

test_cases.test_case: Reset App State clears a populated cart and restores add/remove button states while keeping user logged in
preconditions: User logged in as <Role>
User is on the <App page> where the Reset App State button is visible
Cart contains one or more items; cart badge shows a positive count; at least one product action button shows the 'Remove' state
steps: 1. Click the 'Reset App State' button
test_cases.expected_result: clears cart and resets in-app state (cart badge and add/remove button states) without logging the user out — Cart badge is no longer visible (or shows '0') and the cart contents area shows no items; product action buttons now display the 'Add' state instead of 'Remove'; the user's profile/avatar or account menu remains visible indicating the user is still logged in

test_cases.test_case: Reset App State is idempotent when the cart is already empty and does not log the user out
preconditions: User logged in as <Role>
User is on the <App page> where the Reset App State button is visible
Cart is already empty; cart badge is not visible; product action buttons are in the 'Add' state
steps: 1. Click the 'Reset App State' button
test_cases.expected_result: clears cart and resets in-app state (cart badge and add/remove button states) without logging the user out — Cart remains empty with no cart badge visible; product action buttons remain in the 'Add' state; the user's profile/avatar or account menu remains visible indicating the user is still logged in

test_cases.test_case: Unauthenticated user attempts to press Reset App State
preconditions: User is not authenticated (logged out)
steps: 1. Navigate to the page that contains the Reset App State button
2. Attempt to click the Reset App State button
test_cases.expected_result: User is redirected to the Login page and the Reset App State action is not executed; the cart is not cleared and the cart badge and add/remove button states remain unchanged (no visible UI change from Reset App State).

test_cases.test_case: User without required role attempts to access Reset App State
preconditions: Logged in as <user without the role required to perform Reset App State>
steps: 1. Navigate to the page that normally contains the Reset App State button
2. Look for the Reset App State button (attempt to click it if visible)
test_cases.expected_result: Reset App State button is not visible (or is disabled); the user cannot invoke the action. The cart is not cleared and the cart badge and add/remove button states remain unchanged; the user remains logged in.

test_cases.test_case: Reset with populated cart and toggled add/remove button states
preconditions: User is logged in
Cart contains one or more items
At least one product's add/remove button is showing the 'remove' state
Cart badge is showing a non-zero count
steps: 1. Click the 'Reset App State' button
test_cases.expected_result: Click succeeds; cart is cleared (cart listing shows no items and cart badge is zero or hidden), all add/remove buttons revert to their initial 'add' state, and the user remains logged in (user avatar/menu remains visible). No logout occurs and no error is shown.

test_cases.test_case: Reset when cart is already empty (idempotency)
preconditions: User is logged in
Cart is empty and cart badge is not showing a count
steps: 1. Click the 'Reset App State' button
test_cases.expected_result: Click succeeds; UI remains unchanged for cart (still empty, no items listed), no error or warning is shown, in-app state remains default, and the user remains logged in. The action is idempotent and does not produce a new error or log the user out.

test_cases.test_case: Rapid double-click of Reset App State
preconditions: User is logged in
Cart contains one or more items
Reset App State button is visible and enabled
steps: 1. Click the 'Reset App State' button
2. Immediately click the 'Reset App State' button again (within a short interval)
test_cases.expected_result: First click succeeds and clears the cart; second click is ignored or has no additional effect (no duplicate side effects). The cart remains empty, UI is stable (no error messages), and the user remains logged in. No duplicate state transitions or visible errors occur.

test_cases.test_case: Reset while an in-progress checkout is open
preconditions: User is logged in
User has initiated checkout / is on the checkout page with items in cart
Pay/continue buttons are visible as part of the checkout UI
steps: 1. Click the 'Reset App State' button
test_cases.expected_result: Click succeeds; cart is cleared (checkout UI updates to reflect an empty cart — e.g., no items listed or a clear empty-cart state is shown), checkout actions that require cart items become disabled or indicate empty cart, and the user remains logged in. No logout occurs and no unexpected error is shown.
